titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 62: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 62. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: The framed manuscript page number [ⲝⲃ] (top left) is printed in restoration brackets with a bar above and below as the frame (no strokes); the running title [ⲛⲕⲉⲫⲁⲗⲁⲓⲟⲛ] is restored in brackets, with a stroke over the restored ⲛ. The page is printed pale: dots were located with a scratch blob finder at grey < 140–160 and every run counted on the 4× halves between the bracket positions. Line 1 is "[" + 27 dots (516–1203) at the zone centre, not closed on the page. Reconcile flags explained: on ll. 1, 3, 4, 6–14 and 21 pale dots fall apart into pieces of area < 6 at grey 130 (the counts rest on the zooms and the scratch finder at grey 140–160, §3.20); ll. 15, 19, 23 and 26 have their dot rows at the zone centre, and on 23 and 26 the ϣ bowl dot lies inside the letter's box; l. 5 counts fragments of the pale letters of ⲡⲛⲁ ⲉⲧⲁⲛϩ (817–978) and misses pale dots; l. 16 counts the foot of the bracket (711); l. 18 misses the ϥ dot, joined to its descender (8×); l. 27 counts the margin numeral (470); ll. 29–33 are statements of one line each, not dots (ll. 29, 31 count a piece of the brace and of the German).
Lines 1, 3, 4, 6 and 7 are an opening bracket followed by dots to the line end, never closed: closed at the line end (§4).

Ten dots in the bracket (517–757), eight illegible dots (792–979). In ⲁⲩϣⲁⲣⲥ (pale, broken print) a dot under the first ⲁ (1011, 10× zoom); the specks under ϣ (about 1046–1050, y 393–396) lie on the line of its tail, which in this font curves down to the left, and are not taken as a dot (10×; contrast the round bowl dots of ll. 23, 26); the mark under ⲣ is the foot of its descender. Four dots after the bracket (1191–1270), closed at the line end. No strokes (the bar `strokes` reports at 1129–1139 is the top of ϩ).
"[" + 31 dots (518–1310), closed at the line end.

A raised thick vertical mark (4 px wide, from above the x-height to mid-letter) after ⲡ, inside the restoration bracket: an apostrophe (54.10), so ⲡ[ʼⲣⲏⲧⲉ]. Four illegible dots (638–717). Dot under ⲙ (948). Measured stroke over ⲙⲛ (950–969, pixel row 1448): ⲙ (943–959) 59 %, ⲛ (962–976) 53 %; both. Eleven illegible dots (998–1263).
Lines 29–33 carry no text: one brace beside the margin numerals with "geringe Spuren" → one statement per line (`traces`). Their y-values come from the margin numerals (+3).
Every ϣ on the page was checked at 8–10×: dotted on ll. 23 and 26, undotted on ll. 2, 11, 19.
